quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue within guidance in a mixed market; automotive revenue $116 million down 19% YoY on inventory normalization, industrial $45.2 million down 4% YoY, medical $21 million up 39% YoY; management believes Q2 marked the bottom
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $199.8 million, down 7% year-over-year and up 2% sequentially; EBITDA EUR 33.6 million, margin 16.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance with second half of 2026 expected stronger than the first half; recovery expected to be gradual rather than a quick rebound
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $195 million-$205 million, EBITDA margin 17%-20%

quarterly_data.signal: Underlying book-to-bill ratio returned above 1.0 for the first time since Q2 2024, excluding the temporary impact of the Erfurt end-of-life program; automotive book-to-bill reached its highest level in almost two years
quarterly_data.figure: bookings $173.3 million, up 2% quarter-on-quarter; backlog $291.8 million

quarterly_data.signal: AI-driven data center infrastructure named the most exciting opportunity — power conversion, sensing, infrastructure control, cooling, photonic connectivity, silicon carbide and gallium nitride across all three business units; current data center revenue mostly from silicon carbide, photonics and CMOS
quarterly_data.figure: long-term revenue potential of approximately $300 million annually for data center applications; current data center revenue in the range of $20 million-$30 million

quarterly_data.signal: Wide bandgap revenue growing with three new silicon carbide design wins secured and the gallium nitride roadmap on track; quarterly demand still volatile due to temporary order volatility from a major silicon carbide customer
quarterly_data.figure: wide bandgap revenue $10.6 million, up 34% year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: Microsystems & Photonics growing; progress in co-packaged optics, data communication, AR/VR and quantum-computing-related applications through the LIGENTEC collaboration; photonics volume production expected to start in 2028; awarded EUR 127.4 million under the European Chips Act to expand Microsystems & Photonics manufacturing in Erfurt (Fab4Micro)
quarterly_data.figure: Microsystems & Photonics revenue $28.7 million, up 14% year-over-year; EUR 127.4 million Chips Act award

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity utilization at 60% at the end of Q2, targeting a gradual increase toward 85%-90%; enough capacity in hand for the next two to three years under current growth projections; watching wafer supply tension closely — high demand for SOI wafers and 200 millimeter wafers, with any input price increases to be propagated to customers case by case
